artists.biography:
John Michael "Ozzy" Osbourne (born 3 December 1948) is an English heavy metal vocalist and songwriter, whose musical career has spanned over 40 years. Osbourne rose to prominence as lead singer of the pioneering English band Black Sabbath, whose dark and hard sound helped spawn the heavy metal genre. Due to Sabbath's dark style, Osbourne became known as the "Prince of Darkness". Osbourne is also known as the "Godfather of Heavy Metal".

In the early 2000s, Osbourne's career expanded when he became a star in his own reality show The Osbournes, alongside wife/manager Sharon and two of their three children, Kelly and Jack. A documentary about his life and career, God Bless Ozzy Osbourne, premiered in April 2011 at the Tribeca Film Festival and was released on DVD in November 2011. Osbourne has achieved multi-platinum status as a solo artist and with Black Sabbath and has sold over 100 million albums worldwide.

perplexity.description:
No More Tears is Ozzy Osbourne's sixth studio album, released on September 17, 1991, marking his return after a three-year hiatus from new material. The album showcases heavy metal and progressive rock influences anchored by guitarist Zakk Wylde's grinding riffs and a rawer production approach from producers Duane Baron and John Purdell. Recorded while Osbourne was five months sober—a first for him in the studio—the album represents a creative peak in his solo career, with the band having developed strong chemistry through years of recording and touring together.

The album achieved significant commercial success, reaching number seven on the US Billboard 200 and number 17 on the UK Albums Chart, eventually earning 4x Platinum certification from the RIAA. Three singles achieved Top 10 positions on Billboard's rock charts: the hypnotic title track "No More Tears," the power ballad "Mama, I'm Coming Home," and "Road to Nowhere." The album notably features four co-writing credits from Motörhead frontman Lemmy Kilmister, including on the rare mainstream pop crossover hit "Mama, I'm Coming Home," demonstrating Osbourne's expanded songwriting collaborations during this period.

The album's 11 tracks blend heavy riffs with diverse songwriting, featuring contributions from keyboardist John Sinclair and drummer Randy Castillo alongside Wylde's prominent guitar work. No More Tears successfully positioned Osbourne into the 1990s with some of his strongest solo material, combining the album's raw production sensibility with polished songwriting that resonated with both rock purists and mainstream audiences.
